title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Mimic Panel. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Mimic Panel
options.lineage: industrial SCADA mimic panels and grid control rooms
options.thesis: The network as a physical plant: kill-chain sections as mimic cells that light as the attack advances, the forecast as the plant's trend recorder with a red trip line.
options.viewport: One continuous panel bus: engraved scenario selector, the five ATT&CK cells with the current stage lit amber, the probability timeline drawn across the panel with the alert threshold as a physical trip line.
options.risk: Reads retro-skeuomorphic when engraved detail beats data density.

raised.raise: Absence drawn as deliberately as light: unlit sections are designed ghost states, and numeric readings swap instantly, segment-style, never tween.
Labels set square like stenciled crate plates: every panel zone carries its engraved literal name.
The text field stays achromatic; color lives only in lit cells and data traces, never in chrome.

options.label: Alert Bulletin
options.thesis: The console as an official forecast bulletin: alert levels, probability cones, uncertainty bands - the visual language institutions built for exactly this job of saying what comes next.
options.viewport: A numbered bulletin sheet: issued-time header, the probability cone as the hero graphic, alert level as a stamped severity band.
options.risk: The most intuitive fit for a forecasting product - also the direction most runs in this category land on.

options.label: Segment Display
options.lineage: seven-segment alarm clocks, price totems, scoreboards
options.thesis: Every reading in one eight-cell mask; unlit segments held as ghost cells and every change an instant segment swap.
options.viewport: Peak probability as four bedside-red digits over the timeline; the whole console a rigid mask of cells.
options.case: Fuses cleanly - the peak readout and alert states map naturally to lit/ghost segments - but prose, tables and the ATT&CK chain lose clarity inside a segment mask.
options.risk: Reads novelty when the mask constrains comprehension.

options.label: Quoted Labels
options.lineage: industrial streetwear with zip-tie tags and hazard stripes
options.case: The register fights jury trust: hazard stripes and quoted caps read fashion, not operations.
options.kept: Labels set square like stenciled crate plates - donated to the assigned direction.

options.label: Spectral Fringe
options.lineage: iridescent cloud edges and droplet diffraction
options.case: Pastel fringes read weather-poetry, not security operations; identification fails for a SOC audience.
options.kept: Color confined to hairline data edges over an achromatic text field - donated to the assigned direction.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark SOC dashboard every security product ships: navy glassmorphism panels, neon green/red status, Inter type. Played straight, at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Familiar cockpit: sidebar, cards with glowing accents, chart on top.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other security dashboard by design.
